example_summaries: Brand kept running ads beyond the agreed usage window and creator asks what to charge for continued use.
Advice to bill past overrun usage separately and offer per-video renewal extensions with clear dates.
Platform grants brands unlimited indefinite paid ad usage for a low flat creator fee with no licensing or renewals.
Brands fold ad usage rights into the base creation fee, so creators should price creation and usage separately.
Ad usage and whitelisting are often slipped in for free or tiny budgets despite being the most valuable part of the deal.
Beginner priced year-long paid ad usage separately from creation and the brand declined as over budget.
Pay that only triggers when videos hit a view threshold means there is effectively no guaranteed base rate.
Performance-only offer with no base pay and a view threshold required before any payment.
Advises getting deliverable terms fixed in writing and notes view-only pay shifts all risk to the creator.
Agency keeps all raw footage and can cut multiple videos from one shoot without extra pay.
Once a raw video file is handed over, only the contract can limit its use, so a takedown window should be specified.
Some campaigns demand raw files on top of finished videos for roughly the same fee as a single video.
